lessons.title: Technical Indicator Fundamentals
lessons.description: Reconstruct an indicator value from the bars it was computed from, predict how a longer or shorter lookback changes its responsiveness, identify the warm-up period during which it has no value, and state what market context a signal still needs.

lessons.title: Simple and Exponential Moving Averages
lessons.description: Calculate and compare simple and exponential moving averages, inspect how input source and lookback affect responsiveness, and state when the faster response helps and when it hurts.

lessons.title: Moving Average Trend Filters and Crossovers
lessons.description: Use fast and slow moving averages as a trend-state model, detect crossovers, measure whipsaws, and distinguish a delayed confirmation rule from an early reversal prediction.

lessons.title: Relative Strength Index
lessons.description: Calculate RSI with Wilder smoothing, interpret momentum on a 0–100 scale, test threshold behavior across regimes, and avoid treating overbought or oversold as automatic reversal commands.

lessons.title: Stochastic Oscillator
lessons.description: Measure where the close sits inside its recent high-low range, compare %K and %D smoothing, and explain from the formula why range position pins near an extreme in a trend and turns in a sideways market.

lessons.title: Moving Average Convergence Divergence
lessons.description: Separate the MACD line, signal line, and histogram; change the three periods; identify zero-line and signal-line events; and name what each component measures.

lessons.title: Average Directional Index and Directional Movement
lessons.description: Calculate +DI, −DI, and ADX; distinguish directional dominance from trend strength; adjust the lookback and threshold; and compare the indicator in trending and ranging price series.

lessons.title: Average True Range
lessons.description: Inspect true range components, see how gaps affect volatility measurement, calculate Wilder ATR and ATR as a percentage of price, and keep volatility separate from direction.

lessons.title: Bollinger Bands
lessons.description: Build a moving-average envelope from standard deviation, inspect band width and %B, identify volatility contraction and expansion, and avoid treating a band touch as a complete signal.

lessons.title: Keltner Channels
lessons.description: Construct an EMA-centered ATR envelope, change the basis and volatility settings, compare Keltner Channels with Bollinger Bands, and define channel-break conditions precisely.

lessons.title: Donchian Channels
lessons.description: Track rolling highest highs and lowest lows, compare current-bar and prior-channel calculations, detect completed breakout events, and state which bars define the boundary a close is tested against.

lessons.title: Rate of Change and Momentum
lessons.description: Measure price change over a fixed lookback in percentage and absolute terms, compare zero-line crossings, adjust sensitivity, and distinguish momentum from trend direction and volatility.

lessons.title: Indicator Divergence
lessons.description: Compare aligned price swings with RSI or MACD histogram swings, classify regular bullish and bearish divergence, distinguish divergence from disagreement at unrelated bars, and require price confirmation.

lessons.title: Combining Indicators Without Redundancy
lessons.description: Group indicators by function, compare normalized outputs and correlations, build a compact set for a defined purpose, and avoid stacking multiple transformations of the same price behavior as false confirmation.

lessons.title: Indicator Selection by Market Regime
lessons.description: Classify synthetic market regimes, select indicators suited to the intended decision, receive scored feedback, and justify why the same threshold or crossover is read differently in trends, ranges, contractions, and high volatility.

lessons.title: Indicator-Based Trading Rules
lessons.description: Convert indicator observations into deterministic conditions, apply trend, strength, and volatility filters, visualize entry and exit events, detect contradictory rules, and export a machine-readable specification.
